name: Machine Intelligence Research Institute (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: an AI catastrophe kills people everywhere and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population.
summary: The Machine Intelligence Research Institute (Berkeley) works to prevent extinction from smarter-than-human AI; since 2024 mostly through communications (in 2025 the bestselling book If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies) and governance research on an international halt, with a little technical alignment research. This model covers both programmes in 2025 ($7.7M spent). At the defaults it averts about 0.07 years of healthy life per $1,000, from 0.0003 to 18 on the combined range: each dollar is valued as a typical project's cut in the forecast risk of an AI catastrophe (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model, the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament's experts), with deaths valued like every death and the future lost counted through the discount rate. All its work is against misaligned AI, for which Rethink Priorities' typical project cuts the deaths in catastrophes the world survives far less per dollar than misuse work; the biggest swings are the chance AI ends humanity's future (the slider), the discount rate and that cut per dollar, whose range runs ten times either way. Every branch is discounted for missing data: no outcome of the work on the risk is measured.

rows.label: Research: how far the typical project's effect applies
rows.explainer: MIRI's research against Rethink Priorities' typical small AI project. Below typical: its technical alignment programme, the field's oldest, has little uptake by the labs, and MIRI itself wrote that it grew 'more pessimistic' about it and made policy and communications the priority (2024 strategy update); the Technical Governance Team's 2025 reports (a draft treaty, the technical requirements for a halt, constitutional limits on licensing) were well received but no government has acted on them. 0.7, our judgment, 0.2 to 1.5; anchored on NTI's 0.8, whose diplomacy has a record of governments adopting its products.

source.title: MIRI 2024 Mission and Strategy Update (4 January 2024)
source.quote: it's likely that policy and communications will be a higher priority for MIRI than research going forward

rows.label: Outreach: how far the typical project's effect applies
rows.explainer: MIRI's communications against a typical small AI project. Above typical in reach: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies (September 2025) was an instant New York Times bestseller (#7 on the nonfiction list) and widely reviewed, and MIRI was invited to testify to a committee of the Canadian House of Commons. Below in how directly it acts: a book moves the risk only through opinion and then policy, and its call for an international halt is contested even among people who share the concern (its effect may polarise as well as persuade). 1, our judgment, 0.3 to 2.5, wider than NTI's 0.3 to 1.2 because the reach is large and its effect on policy unknown.

source.title: MIRI's 2025 Fundraiser (MIRI, posted 2 December 2025)
source.quote: It was an instant New York Times bestseller, reaching #7 on the nonfiction list.

rows.label: How far the typical project's effect applies to this charity's work
rows.explainer: How far Rethink Priorities' typical small AI project applies to MIRI's work: research and outreach weighted by their audited spending.

rows.label: Share of the work no one else would have done now
rows.explainer: The share of the work no one else would have done now: other groups communicate AI risk to the public (the Center for AI Safety's 2023 statement, ControlAI, PauseAI) and draft governance proposals (GovAI, RAND, IAPS), but a book by the field's best-known pessimists and the technical drafting of a halt treaty are close to unique. Our judgment, 0.75 (0.4 to 0.95), a little above NTI's 0.7 because fewer groups argue MIRI's position; that the work would have come later is in years_of_impact.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: MIRI's share of the resources behind its work: the book's publisher (Little, Brown) paid for editing, printing and its own marketing, and media and partners gave their time; MIRI paid its authors' salaries, $350,309 of advertising and the launch events. Our judgment, 0.85 (0.6 to 1), as for NTI.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Whether large funders (the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which matched the first $1.6M of the 2025 fundraiser, and the two donors of $12.9M in 2026) would give less if small donors gave more is the room factor of @next_dollar.machine_intelligence_research_institute (docs/normalization.md 2.10), so it isn't asked again here (one question per adjustment): 1, our judgment, as for every catastrophic-risk model; 0.85 to 1.05 for funging the room factor misses.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin: no outcome of MIRI's work on the risk is measured (book sales and media reach are outputs); the cut per dollar is a typical project's from Rethink Priorities' model and the chances are forecasts, so the shared missing-data step applies (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the catastrophes counted: AI Impacts' surveys of AI researchers inform others' forecasts and funding, and the public debate the book started also covers harms short of catastrophe. 5% (0 to 20%) of the modelled value, our judgment, below NTI's 10% (whose materials work lowers terrorism risk that is not modelled).

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: A typical project's chance of backfiring is already in the shared cut per dollar. MIRI's 2025 work builds no capabilities: the governance research argues for halting frontier development and the alignment research is theoretical and unpublished by default. 0, down to -5%. Our judgment.

rows.label: Harm: information hazards and attention, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire: arguments that superintelligence is near and decisive also draw people and money to building it (Keach Hagey's history of OpenAI recounts how Yudkowsky's early writing and introductions helped draw DeepMind's founders and their first investor into the field), and a call for a halt that much of the field rejects can make others' safety proposals look extreme. -5%, down to -30%, our judgment; an attention harm larger than NTI's (0) because mass communication is MIRI's main work.
